title: TikTok Shop Free Samples: A Seller Operations Playbook
summary: Build a TikTok Shop sample program around creator fit, landed cost, fulfillment, content completion, and contribution margin—not shipment volume.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### What is the difference between free, refundable, and targeted samples?


A free sample puts the product and fulfillment cost on the seller. A refundable sample is purchased by the creator and refunded only when the displayed criterion is met. A targeted sample is offered to selected creators inside a Target Collaboration; its payment and content terms still need review.


### How much should a seller budget for samples?


There is no responsible universal percentage. Model landed sample cost, expected product contribution, available inventory, and the learning value of each cohort. Set a loss limit and review it by product.


### How should sellers approve creators?


Use audience and product fit, several relevant content examples, fulfillment history, commercial evidence, quality, and claims risk. Do not depend on follower count or a single platform score.


### What obligations follow an approved sample?


The native order and collaboration terms control. In current US guidance, approved free samples carry shipping and creator-content timelines, while refundable samples use a displayed sales criterion and window. Verify the live account.


### How do sellers measure sample profitability?


Compare cohort contribution and legitimate content value with landed sample and operating cost. Review completion, time to post, returns, attribution limits, and repeat collaboration before expanding a quota.


### Can Reacher change TikTok Shop eligibility or deadlines?


No. Reacher organizes the seller's creator relationships and sample workflow. TikTok Shop controls eligibility, native order status, policy, deadlines, refunds, and platform attribution.
